How the Aurelian Basin is changing

Every place, number and finding on this page is invented for this repository's tests. It imitates the structure of an agency explainer page — nested headings, a data table, a captioned figure — and nothing else.

Observed warming

Basin-mean surface temperature has risen by 1.9 °C since the 1861–1880 baseline. It is very likely that warming will continue through mid-century under every pathway assessed. The lowland record is the longest continuous series in the basin (see Fig. 1).

The lowland record

Lowland stations warmed faster than the coastal shelf (high confidence). It is not likely that station moves explain the difference; homogenisation studies find the effect robust.
